meta.purpose: A decision queue, not a to-do list. Each proposal says what it would change, what it costs, what it risks, whether it can be undone, and which open question must be answered first. A reviewer can approve a row without reading the whole site.
meta.how_to_use: Start with a path, not a row. The three paths below are coherent strategies with different costs and different failure modes; a row only makes sense inside one of them. Then mark each row accept, hold or reject. Decisions are stored in this browser only.
meta.recommended_first: Path A, because it is cheap, reversible, and every other path is worth less until a click is attributed.
meta.honesty_note: Three rows were implemented during the 2026-11-20 build rather than left as proposals, because they were defects rather than choices: tagged destination links, the noindex on the parallel edition, and the thermometer cluster guide. They are kept in the list, marked implemented, so the record shows what changed and why.

paths.name: Prove the money path
paths.summary: Make one attributed click happen, and make the front page ask for it. Nothing about content. Everything about whether this shop can earn at all.
paths.time: Two weeks, most of it waiting for a report to update
paths.signal: A non-zero click count in the Associates report
paths.risk: Low. Every change is reversible and none of it publishes a claim.
paths.gives_up: Nothing, except the illusion that traffic is the problem.
paths.choose_when: You cannot say today whether a click on this site is credited to shopnow047c-20. That is the current state.

paths.name: Publish to measured demand
paths.summary: Switch on Search Console, write from queries people actually typed, keep a dated change log, and set a cadence the operator can hold.
paths.time: Four to eight weeks before the first honest signal
paths.signal: Impressions and query strings in Search Console; a feed subscriber count if anyone subscribes
paths.risk: Medium. Publishing on a cadence with nothing measured yet is how sites fill up with pages nobody asked for.
paths.gives_up: The freedom to write whatever is interesting this week.
paths.choose_when: Path A is closed and you want the fifth guide to be chosen by evidence rather than by instinct.

paths.name: Buy the moat
paths.summary: A named author, one appliance actually bought and used, real photographs, and reader questions collected on purpose. The only path that produces something a competitor cannot copy in an afternoon.
paths.time: Six to twelve weeks, and it needs an evening a week
paths.cash: The price of one appliance, plus a photographer or a phone and a window
paths.signal: Return visits, replies to the one question the site asks, and pages that contain evidence nobody else has
paths.risk: High on effort, low on compliance: testing must really happen before the page exists, and a fake test is the one move that turns this site from careful into deceptive.
paths.gives_up: Speed, and the ability to say 'we publish weekly'.
paths.choose_when: You intend to be here in a year, and you would rather have five pages nobody can match than fifty nobody remembers.

suggestions.title: Click one tagged link, then read the click report
suggestions.why: Program Policies 2(b) requires the tag in the URL. The site now builds it that way. What is still unproven is whether Amazon records the click, and that is the only question standing between this site and earning anything.
suggestions.effort: About ten minutes, plus however long the report takes
suggestions.risk: None. Clicking your own link is a test, not a purchase.
suggestions.recommendation: Do this first

suggestions.title: Offer tagged destination links, and keep the submitted codes as history
suggestions.why: A bare /dp/ address contains no Associates ID, so a click through it cannot be credited and Amazon names untagged links as a rejection reason. Pointing at the listing with the tag attached also makes every link readable in the page source.
suggestions.risk: Low. The submitted link is retained in the record; nothing was deleted.
suggestions.recommendation: Implemented 2026-11-20; verification still required

suggestions.title: Name a real editor, or stop implying editorial authority
suggestions.why: The site says nothing about who wrote it, which a careful reader notices immediately. A named person with an accurate two-sentence bio is the cheapest credibility available, and an invented one would be the most expensive mistake.
suggestions.risk: None, provided the bio describes work that actually happened
suggestions.recommendation: Do within the first month

suggestions.title: Buy, use and photograph one of the three air fryers
suggestions.why: This is the single biggest available jump in both usefulness and ranking potential. Every air-fryer page on the internet is currently assembled from seller copy; a page with a real measurement, a real cleanup test and real photographs would be materially different.
suggestions.risk: Cost. The review must be genuine, so the testing has to happen before the page exists.
suggestions.reversible: No, in the sense that a published test is a commitment
suggestions.recommendation: The highest-value single investment on this list

suggestions.title: Apply for the Product Advertising API before showing any price
suggestions.why: It is the only compliant route to live price, availability and rating, and those are the three things shoppers look for before clicking. Eligibility usually requires qualifying sales, which is what Path A is for.
suggestions.risk: None to the site; the blocker is sequencing
suggestions.recommendation: Start the application after the first attributed click, not before

suggestions.title: Switch on measurement before writing guide number six
suggestions.why: Five guides exist on hypotheses. A sixth written on another hypothesis adds almost nothing. One written from an actual query report adds a page with a reason to exist.
suggestions.effort: An hour of setup, then two to four weeks of waiting
suggestions.risk: Low. The client is already written and stays silent until switched on.
suggestions.reversible: Yes, it can be switched off
suggestions.recommendation: Do before more content

suggestions.title: Verify the property in Search Console and submit the sitemap
suggestions.why: Without this the site cannot be found, and the topic question can never be answered with data. It is also the only free, first-party source of the queries the site is already appearing for.
suggestions.risk: None. Requires the owner's Google account, so it cannot be done by an agent.
suggestions.recommendation: Do this week

suggestions.title: Decide whether the thermometers are a line or an accessory
suggestions.why: Two of the five products are thermometers, in the same Amazon category path. That is either a coherent second cluster or a distraction, and the difference decides the navigation.
suggestions.risk: None
suggestions.recommendation: Answer before the next guide is written

suggestions.title: Add one reader question capture, with the privacy notice written first
suggestions.why: The most reliable source of missing information is the reader. A single question field produces the queries no keyword tool shows, but it also creates a data obligation that must exist before the field does.
suggestions.effort: An hour plus a provider decision
suggestions.risk: Medium: consent, retention and who answers replies
suggestions.recommendation: Do after Path A, and only with a written notice

suggestions.title: Publish a dated change log on the site
suggestions.why: The site changes its product record, its flags and its sources. A dated list of what changed and why is the cheapest evidence of maintenance, and it gives a returning reader a reason to return.
suggestions.risk: None, provided every entry is true
suggestions.recommendation: Start with the 2026-11-20 session

suggestions.title: Do not commission more AI-written guides until S-04 or S-06 lands
suggestions.why: More synthetic prose makes the site bigger, not better, and it raises the chance the whole publication is judged as one undifferentiated block. The five existing guides are defensible because they claim little; that advantage survives by not being diluted.
suggestions.effort: None. It is a decision not to do something.
suggestions.risk: None
suggestions.recommendation: Agree this in writing

suggestions.title: Replace illustrations with the operator's own photographs
suggestions.why: Every image here is generated and labelled as such. Labelled illustration is honest; it is also the thing a reader weighs when deciding whether a shop is real.
suggestions.effort: A phone camera and an afternoon
suggestions.risk: None, provided the photo is of the product being discussed
suggestions.recommendation: Do it the moment one product is bought

suggestions.title: Put the shortlist above the method on the front page
suggestions.why: A shop shows the goods first. The current front page spends a hero and a three-card explainer before a single product appears, which is the shape of an audit rather than a shop.
suggestions.risk: Low. It changes the order of sections, not the claims.
suggestions.recommendation: Test it against the current order once clicks are counted

suggestions.title: Make the two thermometers a decision, not a footnote
suggestions.why: An instant-read probe and a wireless multi-probe set solve different problems at different prices. That is a genuinely useful comparison, and the site now has the verified identities to write it without inventing anything.
suggestions.risk: Low: every attribute is quoted as the seller's wording
suggestions.recommendation: Implemented 2026-11-20

suggestions.title: Build one dated seasonal hub that makes no price claim
suggestions.why: Seasonal shopping is when affiliate traffic actually arrives, and a hub can be useful without a single price: what to measure, what to check before the sales, what to ignore. It also gives the feed something to publish in a quiet month.
suggestions.effort: Two evenings, once a year per season
suggestions.risk: Medium: seasonal pages go stale and must say when they were written
suggestions.recommendation: Do before the next gifting season, dated in the title

suggestions.title: Give search engines one site: noindex the parallel edition
suggestions.why: Two editions of the same shop were built in parallel and both are served. Duplicate copies of the same product pages split whatever signal exists and confuse a reader who lands on the other one.
suggestions.risk: Low. noindex is reversible and no URL breaks; nothing was deleted.
suggestions.recommendation: Implemented 2026-11-20; owner may still choose redirect or delete

suggestions.title: Publish to Amazon's own ten-post originality bar, deliberately
suggestions.why: Amazon says sites must have robust original content, even with advertising removed, and gives ten posts as a rule of thumb. The site has the count and not the depth; knowing the bar is the first step to clearing it on purpose.
suggestions.risk: High if ignored: a rejected application cannot be reassessed
suggestions.recommendation: Do the audit before any application or re-application

suggestions.title: Ask five real buyers five questions and publish what they say
suggestions.why: Almost every unknown in the decision register is an intent question no research tool can answer: whether the thermometers belong, what a reader wants first, why someone would return. Five conversations close more of them than a month of keyword work.
suggestions.effort: Five conversations and an hour of writing
suggestions.risk: Low, if what they say is reported accurately and with permission
suggestions.recommendation: The cheapest way to discover missing information

suggestions.title: Schedule a monthly link-integrity pass and record it
suggestions.why: One supplied link failed three times in one session and resolved twice in this one. Flakiness like that is invisible without a record, and a dead affiliate link earns nothing while looking perfectly fine.
suggestions.effort: Ten minutes a month, or an hour to automate
suggestions.risk: None
suggestions.recommendation: Do it manually first, automate only if it sticks

suggestions.title: Set a cadence the operator can actually hold, and put it on the site
suggestions.why: A publication has a rhythm. Two guides a month, dated, drawn from measured queries, is sustainable; 'we publish weekly' on a site with no author and no testing is the kind of claim that quietly turns into a lie.
suggestions.risk: Low, if the cadence is honest
suggestions.recommendation: Do after Path A
